tagline: Rubber, hype and limited drops: why people queue overnight for shoes.
why: Sneaker culture turned sports shoes into collectibles, fashion statements and an investment market. It's tied to basketball, hip-hop, skateboarding and streetwear, and a few brands release limited models that sell out in seconds and resell for many times their price. Hong Kong has a famous sneaker street and a strong streetwear scene, so shoes are an easy, fun topic.

essentials.title: Drops and hype
essentials.body: Brands release limited 'drops' through apps and raffles. Demand far exceeds supply, so shoes resell above retail on platforms like StockX and GOAT.

essentials.title: Nike rules, but it's shifting
essentials.body: Nike (with Jordan Brand) dominates. But in the 2020s, running brands like On and Hoka and retro styles from Adidas and New Balance have stolen attention.

essentials.title: Collaborations drive heat
essentials.body: Collabs with designers and celebrities, like Travis Scott, Off-White's Virgil Abloh, or Sacai, create the most wanted shoes.

essentials.title: Silhouettes are the models
essentials.body: Collectors talk in silhouettes: Air Jordan 1, Air Force 1, Dunk, Air Max, Yeezy Boost, Samba, 550. Each has many colourways.

essentials.title: Condition is everything
essentials.body: 'Deadstock' (unworn) shoes in the original box hold value. Worn ones drop sharply.

essentials.title: Trends cycle fast
essentials.body: Chunky 'dad shoes', then slim terrace shoes like the Adidas Samba, then running shoes as fashion. What's hot changes every year or two.

names.name: Michael Jordan / Air Jordan
names.what: The 1985 Air Jordan 1 launched modern sneaker culture.

names.name: Nike
names.what: The giant behind Air Max, Air Force 1, Dunk and more.

names.name: Adidas
names.what: German rival; Stan Smith, Superstar, Samba and Gazelle are classics.

names.name: New Balance
names.what: Once 'dad shoes', now fashionable thanks to the 550, 990 and collaborations.

names.name: Virgil Abloh
names.what: Off-White founder and Louis Vuitton designer whose 2017 'The Ten' Nike collab is legendary. Died in 2021.

names.name: Travis Scott
names.what: Rapper whose reversed-swoosh Jordans are some of the most wanted shoes.

names.name: Kanye West / Yeezy
names.what: The Yeezy line with Adidas was huge until Adidas ended the deal in 2022 over his antisemitic comments.

names.name: On
names.what: Swiss running brand with 'cloud' soles, now worn everywhere.

names.name: Hoka
names.what: Maximal-cushion running shoes that became fashionable.

names.name: Asics
names.what: Japanese brand whose retro Gel models are popular with fashion crowds.

names.name: Onitsuka Tiger
names.what: Asics' heritage line, hugely popular with tourists in Asia.

names.name: StockX
names.what: The 'stock market of sneakers', a resale platform.

names.name: Edison Chen / CLOT
names.what: Hong Kong star whose streetwear brand CLOT has done famous Nike collabs.

timeline.event: Converse All Star launches; Chuck Taylor later becomes its face.
Air Jordan 1 is released and banned (so the story goes) by the NBA.
Run-DMC's 'My Adidas' links sneakers and hip-hop.
Nike Air Max 1 shows visible air cushioning.
Pigeon Dunk release causes a near-riot in New York.
Yeezy Boost 350 launches; resale culture explodes.
Dunk mania and pandemic resale peak.
Adidas Samba becomes the shoe of the year.
Running brands On and Hoka grow fast as Nike struggles and resets.

now.headline: Nike's comeback attempt
now.detail: After sales slowed, a new CEO is refocusing on running and sport rather than endless retro drops.

now.headline: Resale has cooled
now.detail: Many hyped shoes now sell near retail. Only the rarest collabs still command big premiums.

now.headline: Running shoes as fashion
now.detail: On, Hoka, Asics and Salomon are worn as everyday shoes.

now.headline: Slim shoes are back
now.detail: Low-profile shoes like the Samba, Puma Speedcat and Onitsuka Tiger Mexico 66 are in fashion.

now.headline: Tariffs
now.detail: Most sneakers are made in Vietnam, China and Indonesia, so trade tariffs push prices up.

local.headline: Sneakers Street
local.detail: Fa Yuen Street in Mong Kok is lined with sneaker shops and is famous across Asia.

local.headline: Hong Kong hype
local.detail: Queues for drops at shops like Juice and Nike's Causeway Bay store are a local ritual.

local.headline: CLOT and Edison Chen
local.detail: CLOT's Nike collabs, such as the 'Silk' Air Force 1, are local legends.

local.headline: Onitsuka Tiger queues
local.detail: Tourists queue for Onitsuka Tiger shoes in Hong Kong and Japan.

debates.question: Is resale culture ruining sneakers?
debates.sides: Bots and resellers make it hard for real fans to buy; others say it's a fair market.

debates.question: Should you wear expensive sneakers?
debates.sides: Some keep them deadstock; others say shoes are meant to be worn.

debates.question: Is Nike losing its cool?
debates.sides: Smaller brands are hot, but Nike still dominates and has a deep archive.
